parsed.explanation: The combined regime is bifurcated. Federal entry, document, facility-funding and custody rules are the operative hazards: binary-sex passport/visa policy, X-marker refusal, sex-discrepancy screening, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, and documented abuse in immigration/national custody. Division-level anti-discrimination, X state IDs, commission remedies and a city sanctuary make daily life and adult care comparatively safer once inside. A traveller whose foreign documents raise a sex discrepancy can be refused or detained before reaching those local protections; minors face federal care and school-threat framing plus local youth protections. The documented federal universal exposures and custody harm place this in Elevated Risk, not Reduced, while local protection prevents a High/Severe floor.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex passport/visa policy; X markers no longer processed for new issues; cable treats sex discrepancy as reasonable doubt, permits refusal, extra evidence, and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. Eight governments issued advisories. Existing X passports valid only until expiry.
entry_documents.protection: Pending litigation and a legal-aid FAQ; division X IDs and anti-discrimination law do not reach the federal border.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passports are checked by federal officers; state protections cannot override federal entry screening or visa fraud findings.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Suspected document/sex misrepresentation can lead to immigration detention; reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse. National corrections use conversion practices including hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution, and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some executive orders are enjoined; no documented operative shield in federal immigration or corrections custody. City sanctuary is limited to city resources and care enforcement.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border discrepancy can move the traveller into federal detention/custody, outside division control.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; some states criminalise bathroom use, with a documented arrest. Division has no such state ban.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division anti-discrimination, commission enforcement, city gender-neutral bathroom requirements, and sanctuary policies.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding/facility rules can reach nationally funded sites; local rules govern state and private venues.

care_services.exposure: National rules target gender-affirming care for minors and reimbursement; custody denies hormones; national health agencies purge related terms. Division adult care is lawful with no adult ban documented.
care_services.protection: Division regulations define sex to include gender identity; anti-discrimination enforcement; largest city sanctuary for gender-affirming care; local conversion-therapy funding ban.
care_services.interaction: City sanctuary shields local care from outside enforcement, but federal funding, insurance rules and custody exposure remain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice reward guidance and hostile agency rhetoric. State hate-crime law does not cover anti-LGBTQ violence.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute; division commission investigates discrimination; city sanctuary and local ordinances.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises climate and targeting risk; local police and protections partly buffer inside the division but cannot control federal agencies.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders call minor gender-affirming care mutilation, bar reimbursement, and direct investigation/prosecution of school staff facilitating social transition. Document mismatch at the border also affects minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Division youth-serving organisation protections, city school X markers, local conversion-therapy bans, and no documented state minor-care ban.
minors_guardians.interaction: Federal funding and school directives sit above local rules; a short visit reduces school exposure but care, medication and border risk remain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide hate-crime law reaches anti-LGBTQ violence; national climate is hostile. No documented pattern of visitor-targeted violence in the division.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute; division anti-discrimination commission; city sanctuary and local ordinances.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local recourse exists for discrimination, but the hate-crime gap and federal climate weaken the overall response.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, executive-order challenges and health rules remain unresolved; fraud waiver is limited; federal custody oversight is weak. Some orders are enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation, legal-aid FAQ, division commission remedies including stop orders, training and damages, and city sanctuary.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies vary by stage: local remedies work in the division, while federal border and custody remedies remain uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a blanket visitor conduct register excluding trans travellers. This dossier lacks a blanket trans-entry ban and has a protective division, but federal document mismatch can trigger refusal, lifetime fraud ineligibility and abusive custody. Slightly above 0.35-A, still high risk.

0.45-B restricts nonresident education and care with no imprisonment. This dossier has comparable uneven service access and stronger local anti-discrimination, but adds federal entry refusal and custody abuse. Roughly similar, with more severe federal exposure.

0.55-B involves extended secondary screening and administrative refusal without criminal prosecution. This dossier adds possible lifetime fraud ineligibility and documented federal custody harm, so it sits below 0.55-B despite division-level protections.

0.75-C has trained border officers, matching passports, brief detention and tribunal review. This dossier's federal binary-sex entry regime and custody record are materially worse, so it rates far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The federal layer supplies the traveller-facing hazards: binary-sex documents, X-marker refusal, sex-discrepancy screening, possible permanent fraud ineligibility and abusive immigration/national custody. The division layer supplies real but bounded mitigation: anti-discrimination enforcement, X state IDs, adult care legality, city sanctuary and local facility inclusion. A visitor whose foreign passport or visa file raises a sex discrepancy meets the federal gate before any local protection; once inside the division, ordinary services and adult care are safer. Minors face federal care and school-threat framing plus local youth protections. The net is Elevated Risk: local protection prevents a High/Severe floor, but federal universal exposures and custody harm block Reduced Risk.
